analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Enterprises is an incoherent conglomerate — steel trading, real estate, mining, engineering, and pizza outlets — with a near-zero operating track record before 2022, ROE of just 2.48%, and earnings overwhelmingly driven by non-operational "Other Income" rather than business fundamentals. At 78x EV/EBITDA for a 6% operating margin steel trader, the valuation is absurd.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.16 is conservative — borrowings manageable at current scale
Revenue has grown sharply from INR 1 Cr (2021) to INR 1,488 Cr (2025) — business is clearly at an inflection
key_risks: Earnings quality is fraudulent-looking: FY22 net profit INR 154 Cr on INR 48 Cr revenue — Other Income INR 159 Cr dominated; FY24 similar (Other Income INR 135 Cr vs operating income INR 89 Cr)
Balance sheet exploded from INR 2,396 Cr to INR 5,582 Cr in one year with borrowings jumping from INR 125 Cr to INR 671 Cr — aggressive debt-funded expansion with no operational track record
Business model is completely incoherent — steel, real estate, mining, engineering, and pizza in one entity with no identifiable core competency
red_flags: Company was called 'Shree Global Tradefin Limited' until September 2023 — a name change and reinvention is a classic red flag
Revenue was literally INR 1 Cr in FY2020 and FY2021 — this is not a mature business, it is being constructed in real time
ROE of 2.48% and ROCE of 5.97% are dismal — below cost of capital; the business destroys value operationally
EV/EBITDA of 78x for a steel trading and real estate conglomerate is extreme market speculation, not investment
OCF was negative in 2 of last 5 years; free cash flow near zero — business consumes more cash than it generates
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my perspective, Lloyds Enterprises is not a business — it is a story. Revenue of INR 1 Cr in FY2020 growing to INR 1,488 Cr in FY2025 is not organic compounding; it is business reconstruction, and I do not know what I am really buying. The net profits are a mirage: FY2022 showed INR 154 Cr profit on INR 48 Cr revenue only because Other Income was INR 159 Cr. FY2024 showed INR 175 Cr profit with Other Income of INR 135 Cr against just INR 89 Cr operating income. A business where earnings consistently come from financial investments, asset sales, or one-time items — not from operations — is not a business I can value or trust. Operating margin of 6% on a steel trading model is structurally weak.

The balance sheet tells a concerning story of rapid, debt-funded scale-up: total assets doubled from INR 2,396 Cr to INR 5,582 Cr in FY2025 alone, with borrowings jumping from INR 125 Cr to INR 671 Cr — a 5x increase in one year. CWIP jumped to INR 132 Cr, suggesting aggressive capital deployment. I built DMart over decades by staying focused, keeping debt near zero, and only expanding when I understood the economics deeply. This company spans steel, real estate, mining, engineering, and pizza outlets — there is no focused operator here. At 78x EV/EBITDA with 2.48% ROE, the market is pricing in a transformation that the fundamentals do not support. Hard pass.
